summary:
Our project focuses on identifying and evaluating potential landing sites on the Moon and Mars, considering both landing safety and scientific research opportunities.

We selected seven regions: Mare Tranquillitatis, Shackleton–de Gerlache Connecting Ridge, Copernicus Crater, Jezero Crater, Elysium Planitia, Argyre Basin, and Alba Mons.

Our methodology began with visual examination of 3D planetary maps to identify potentially suitable terrain. We then used scientific mapping resources, including LOLA and MOLA, alongside elevation, slope, temperature, solar illumination, gravity, and geological data to assess each region.

We also investigated geological characteristics and potential mineral resources to understand the scientific value of each location. Based on preliminary topographic observations, we identified candidate coordinates near the selected regions that appeared relatively flat and potentially more suitable for landing.

Finally, we compared all seven regions in terms of landing suitability, mineral potential, and overall scientific value. The project highlights the opportunities and challenges of different lunar and Martian environments and provides a preliminary assessment to support future planetary exploration.
details: Identifying Suitable Landing Sites on the Moon and Mars Our project focuses on identifying and evaluating potential landing sites on the Moon and Mars, considering both landing safety and scientific research opportunities. Methodology We began by examining 3D planetary maps to identify regions with potentially flat terrain and favorable elevation. We then used scientific mapping resources, including LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter), MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter), LROC, NASA Moon Trek, and Mars Trek. Our evaluation considered several factors, including surface slope, elevation, temperature, solar illumination, local gravity, geological characteristics, and potential mineral resources. We also examined possible landing hazards such as steep terrain, craters, and uneven surfaces. Selected Regions We investigated seven regions: - Moon: Mare Tranquillitatis, Shackleton–de Gerlache Connecting Ridge, and Copernicus Crater. - Mars: Jezero Crater, Elysium Planitia, Argyre Basin, and Alba Mons. For each region, we examined its geological characteristics, landing conditions, and scientific value. We also identified nearby candidate coordinates that appeared relatively flat and potentially suitable for further investigation. Comparative Assessment The seven regions were compared based on landing suitability, mineral potential, and overall assessment. This allowed us to identify the advantages and limitations of different planetary environments. Future Work Further high-resolution topographic analysis, surface hazard mapping, and investigation of subsurface resources would help verify the candidate coordinates and improve the accuracy of our assessment. Our project provides a preliminary comparative evaluation of potential landing regions and demonstrates how planetary datasets can support future exploration of the Moon and Mars.
